title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's July 1986 notes on 'ateliers', an axiomatic framework he was developing for a 'géométrie des formes' and a tame ('modérée') topology. The previous page classifies kinds of ateliers (spatial, faithful, 'lozal', moderate, discrete, ...). This page opens a fresh start ('la réflexion a tendance à s'enliser') and builds the basic one-dimensional model of a 'continuum' from an arbitrary ordered set.

Construction. Let L be a poset. Define M = M_0 ⊔ M_1:
- M_0 = L, the 'vertices' or 'lieux' (points).
- M_1 = Drap_2(L), the 2-element chains {a<b}. Each is viewed as an 'interval' I_{a,b} (also written I_{b,a}).

Supports, boundaries and incidence.
- Support: |x| = {x} and |I_{a,b}| = [a,b] = {x ∈ L : a ≤ x ≤ b}.
- Boundary: ∂I_{a,b} = {a,b} and ∂x = ∅.
- 'Closed boundary' δ: δI_{a,b} = {a,b} and δx = {x}.
- Incidence X ◁ Y holds exactly when X is a point x, Y is an interval, and x ∈ ∂Y. Hence ∂X = {Y : Y ◁ X}, so ∂ is the boundary operator of this incidence.

The resulting structure is a 1-dimensional cell complex with cells = points and nondegenerate closed intervals of L. Unlike the 1-skeleton of the order complex, all intervals appear, not just covering pairs.

The relation ≪ (inclusion of supports).
- X ≪ Y ⟺ |X| ⊂ |Y|. This is the poset of all nonempty closed intervals of L ordered by inclusion: [a,b] determines a and b as its min and max, so |·| is injective.
- It splits into two mutually exclusive parts: boundary incidence ◁, and a 'strict/interior' inclusion ˚≪.
- ˚≪ means: X = Y; or a point strictly inside an interval (a<x<b); or a subinterval (a' ≤ a < b ≤ b').
- Hence: x ≪ I_{a,b} iff a ≤ x ≤ b, and I_{a,b} ≪ I_{a',b'} iff a' ≤ a < b ≤ b'.
- Remark: X ≪ Y implies δX ∪ δY is a chain (flag) of L.
- The margin 'Relation d'ordre Mag 2, OK' checks one of the axioms ('Mag 1–4') of the structure he is axiomatizing.

A bracketed self-criticism says it would have been better to first put an order ≤ on M itself, with points and intervals interleaved (a < I_{a,b} < b). The next page does exactly this, defines |∘| ('comparable for <'), and verifies Mag 3 and Mag 4.

Purpose: to exhibit, from any ordered set, a model 'atelier' of a 1-dimensional continuum (the ordered line cut into points and open cells), as a test case for the axioms.
errors: First displayed definition: read literally as 'X ≪ Y ⟺ |X|⊂|Y| and X ⋪ Y', it conflicts with the later decomposition ≪ = ◁ ⊔ ˚≪. It is evidently the definition of ˚≪ (the circle accent is faint or misread); with that reading everything is consistent.

The 'Conséquence' relation 'X ≪^b Y ⟺ ∃Y', X ˚≪ Y' ◁ Y' degenerates as written. Y' ◁ Y forces Y' to be a point, so X ˚≪ Y' forces X = Y', and the relation is just ◁. The intended composite is presumably X ◁ Y' ˚≪ Y (endpoint of a subinterval), whose union with ˚≪ gives ≪. A minor slip.
Margin note 'δX ⊄ ∂X, ∂X ⊂ δX' is only partly right: for points ∂x = ∅ ⊂ δx = {x}, but for intervals ∂ = δ. Harmless.

When L is not a chain, [a,b] may contain incomparable elements. The statements on this page remain correct, but the 'interval' picture of a line segment presupposes L totally ordered (or the restriction to chains made by the flag condition).

ideas.what: From a poset L, build a 1-dimensional cell structure M = L ⊔ Drap_2(L) (points and intervals) with boundary maps and an incidence relation.
ideas.modern_name: 1-dimensional cell/face poset; cell decomposition of an ordered line (cf. o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1); interval poset of L
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorial topology; o-minimal 1-dim cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is programmatically announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'ateliers' formalism is unpublished.

ideas.what: Decomposition of support inclusion ≪ into boundary incidence ◁ and interior inclusion ˚≪ (mutually exclusive), plus the remark that comparable cells have endpoints forming a flag.
ideas.modern_name: Face relation vs. 'interior' inclusion in a regular cell complex; closed vs. open cells

ideas.what: Using this model to test axioms 'Mag 1–4' of the 'atelier' notion meant to formalize a continuum for tame topology.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / combinatorial models of the continuum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's program (Esquisse, 1984); o-minimality as the realized form

missed.claim: The 'ateliers' program, an axiomatic combinatorial framework for a 'continuum' and tame topology (sketched in Esquisse), is developed in these 1986 notes with explicit axioms (Mag 1–4) and the order-based 1-dim model. It was never published or taken up; o-minimality developed independently with a model-theoretic rather than combinatorial-axiomatic foundation. This page itself contains only the routine 1-dim model.
missed.quote: La réflexion a tendance à s'enliser, et j'ai envie de tout reprendre, d'une façon un peu différente.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for comparing Grothendieck's own attempt at tame topology with o-minimal structures and with combinatorial approaches (stratified spaces, exit paths, posets as finite spaces). The mathematics on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine construction of a 1-dimensional cell model (points and intervals) from an ordered set, with elementary verifications. Its only interest is as part of the little-known, unpublished 'ateliers' program for tame topology.
transcription_corrections: The underlined word in 'ensemble des "moments" initiaux' looks more like '"sommets" initiaux, ou "lieux"'.
The first displayed relation definition should likely read 'X ˚≪ Y ⟺ |X|⊂|Y| et X ⋪ Y' (circle accent), consistent with the case list that follows.
Remark line: the relation appears as '≪' with something crossed out above it: 'X ≪ Y ⟹ δX ∪ δY ∈ Drap(L)'.

The bracketed note reads roughly: 'Il semble qu'il aurait mieux valu introduire d'abord la relation ≤ dans M, d'interpréter I_{a,b}, I_{a,·}, I_{·,b} comme des "intervalles" dans M, et les ... [sous-ensembles?] ...]', anticipating the order on M defined on the next page.
The left-margin note near the top is uncertain; it seems to add a condition on L (connected, possibly a cardinality condition), not 'graphe' commentary.
